question: Which RRC state is the UE in when no RRC connection is established?
gold_chunks: A UE is either in RRC_CONNECTED state or in RRC_INACTIVE state when an RRC connection has been established. If this is not the case, i.e. no RRC connection is established, the UE is in RRC_IDLE state.

question: In RRC_IDLE, does the UE monitor a Paging channel for CN paging using 5G-S-TMSI?
gold_chunks: RRC_IDLE: A UE specific DRX may be configured by upper layers; UE controlled mobility based on network configuration; The UE: Monitors Short Messages transmitted with P-RNTI over DCI; Monitors a Paging channel for CN paging using 5G-S-TMSI; Performs neighbouring cell measurements and cell (re-)selection; Acquires system information and can send SI request (if configured).

question: Does the UE store the UE Inactive AS context in RRC_INACTIVE?
gold_chunks: RRC_INACTIVE: A UE specific DRX may be configured by upper layers or by RRC layer; UE controlled mobility based on network configuration; The UE stores the UE Inactive AS context; A RAN-based notification area is configured by RRC layer.

question: Does the UE discard the UE Inactive AS context while remaining in RRC_INACTIVE?
gold_answer: No. The context is stored in RRC_INACTIVE; it is discarded when the UE leaves RRC_INACTIVE for RRC_IDLE.
gold_chunks: RRC_INACTIVE: ... The UE stores the UE Inactive AS context ...

If the UE is leaving RRC_INACTIVE: ... discard the UE Inactive AS context, if any; release the suspendConfig, if configured; ... enter RRC_IDLE and perform cell selection as specified in TS 38.304 [20].

question: What logical channel is used by SRB0 for RRC messages?
gold_chunks: Signalling Radio Bearers (SRBs) are defined as Radio Bearers (RBs) that are used only for the transmission of RRC and NAS messages. More specifically, the following SRBs are defined: SRB0 is for RRC messages using the CCCH logical channel.

question: Does the RRC protocol provide notification of UEs in RRC_IDLE, for example about a mobile terminating call?
gold_chunks: The RRC protocol offers the following services to upper layers: Broadcast of common control information; Notification of UEs in RRC_IDLE, e.g. about a mobile terminating call; Notification of UEs about ETWS and/or CMAS; Transfer of dedicated signalling.

question: Does SRB2 have a lower priority than SRB1?
gold_chunks: SRB2 is for NAS messages, all using DCCH logical channel. SRB2 has a lower priority than SRB1 and may be configured by the network after AS security activation.

question: What is the purpose of the paging procedure?
gold_answer: To transmit paging information to a UE in RRC_IDLE or RRC_INACTIVE.

question: When T300 expires, does the UE reset MAC, release the MAC configuration, and re-establish RLC for established RBs?
gold_chunks: The UE shall: if timer T300 expires: reset MAC, release the MAC configuration and re-establish RLC for all RBs that are established.

question: Is the purpose of RRC connection resume to resume a suspended RRC connection, including resuming SRBs and DRBs, or perform an RNA update?
gold_chunks: The purpose of this procedure is to resume a suspended RRC connection, including resuming SRB(s) and DRB(s) or perform an RNA update.

question: Does TS 38.300 define an NG-RAN node as only a gNB?
gold_answer: No. An NG-RAN node can be a gNB or an ng-eNB.
gold_chunks: An NG-RAN node is either: a gNB, providing NR user plane and control plane protocol terminations towards the UE; or an ng-eNB, providing E-UTRA user plane and control plane protocol terminations towards the UE.

question: Is NG-U defined between the NG-RAN node and the AMF?
gold_answer: No. NG-U is defined between the NG-RAN node and the UPF.
gold_chunks: The NG user plane interface (NG-U) is defined between the NG-RAN node and the UPF. The transport network layer is built on IP transport and GTP-U is used on top of UDP/IP to carry the user plane PDUs between the NG-RAN node and the UPF. NG-U provides non-guaranteed delivery of user plane PDUs between the NG-RAN node and the UPF.

question: Does NG-U provide guaranteed delivery of user-plane PDUs?
gold_answer: No. NG-U provides non-guaranteed delivery of user plane PDUs.
gold_chunks: NG-U provides non-guaranteed delivery of user plane PDUs between the NG-RAN node and the UPF.

question: Is the Xn-U interface defined between two NG-RAN nodes?
gold_chunks: The Xn User plane (Xn-U) interface is defined between two NG-RAN nodes. The user plane protocol stack on the Xn interface is shown in Figure 4.3.2.1-1. The transport network layer is built on IP transport and GTP-U is used on top of UDP/IP to carry the user plane PDUs.

question: In RRC_INACTIVE, is paging initiated by the 5GC rather than NG-RAN?
gold_answer: No. Paging is initiated by NG-RAN (RAN paging).

question: In RRC_CONNECTED, is the UE AS context stored only in the UE?
gold_answer: No. It is stored in NG-RAN and the UE.
gold_chunks: RRC_CONNECTED: 5GC - NG-RAN connection (both C/U-planes) is established for UE; The UE AS context is stored in NG-RAN and the UE; NG-RAN knows the cell which the UE belongs to; Transfer of unicast data to/from the UE; Transfer of MBS multicast/broadcast data to the UE over MRB(s); Network controlled mobility including measurements.

question: Does the MIB contain cell barred status information and essential physical-layer information needed to receive further system information?
gold_chunks: MIB contains cell barred status information and essential physical layer information of the cell required to receive further system information, e.g. CORESET#0 configuration. MIB is periodically broadcast on BCH.

question: Is SIB1 also referred to as Remaining Minimum SI (RMSI)?
gold_chunks: SIB1 defines the scheduling of other system information blocks and contains information required for initial access. SIB1 is also referred to as Remaining Minimum SI (RMSI) and can either be periodically broadcast on DL-SCH, sent in a dedicated manner on DL-SCH to UEs in RRC_CONNECTED, or broadcast on-demand upon OD-SIB1 request from UEs in RRC_IDLE, RRC_INACTIVE or RRC_CONNECTED state when T311 is running if a UE and cell support OD-SIB1.

question: Does the BAP sublayer use configured mapping to derive an egress BH RLC channel from the ingress BH RLC channel when routing a packet from ingress to egress?
gold_answer: Yes. The IAB-node derives the egress BH RLC channel through an F1AP-configured mapping from the BH RLC channel used on the ingress BH link.
gold_chunks: When routing a packet from an ingress to an egress BH link, the IAB-node derives the egress BH RLC channel on the egress BH link through an F1AP-configured mapping from the BH RLC channel used on the ingress BH link. The BH-RLC-channel IDs used for ingress and egress BH RLC channels are generated by the IAB-donor-CU. Since the BH RLC channel ID only has link-local scope, the mapping configurations also include the BAP addresses of prior and next hop.
